reason:
The headline claim is disproven by the only output that is the artifact. I rendered state=print to A4 PDF (page.pdf, format A4, zero margins) from a 640px-wide window and from a 1440px-wide window: both files are 36,766 bytes and differ in exactly two bytes - the seconds digit of /CreationDate and /ModDate. Every content byte is identical. Chromium lays the sheet out at the paper width (794 CSS px) when it prints, so '@media (min-width: 701px)' and '@container (min-width: 600px)' both match on paper, always. The printed keepsake sets the count at 148, the ceremonial date at 30, the gutter figure at 17 and two columns at 220px + rest, from any window. Geometry and type do not disagree about how wide the document is; they agree, at the only width the document has.

The measured screen numbers in the finding are correct (96/20/15 below 701, 148/30/17 at and above; I reproduced them at 640/700/701/900/1440), but what they measure is the LAB'S stage, not the sheet. shell.css:270 caps [data-medium="sheet"] .tl-stage at 794px - A4 at 96dpi. At 1440 the .b-print box measures 792px and the preview IS the printed page. The preview only diverges when the reviewer's own window is narrower than a sheet of A4, i.e. when the stage can no longer show the artifact at size. That is a property of previewing a fixed physical object in a too-small window, not a property of the object.

The fix would make it worse. The three font-sizes named are not the only things in that '@media (min-width: 701px)' block that dress the sheet: the measure geometry is there too - '.b-measure { padding-left: 124px }', '.b-rail { left: 100px }', '.b-item/.b-origin { left: 124px }', and on the same line as the font-size the finding wants to move, '.b-away { left: -124px; width: 84px }'. Moving only the type into '@container (min-width: 600px)' leaves the lane where it is and re-creates the exact disagreement the finding is named for, inverted: at a 701-790px window the .b-print container measures ~507px, so the sheet would set a 15px figure in a viewport-positioned 84px lane and a 96px count in a 124px lane. Curing it properly means moving the whole measure geometry to the container query - a large edit to two passing gates that changes nothing at all in the printed artifact.

The dead rule is real and inert. '.b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body) }' at b.css:1255 is indeed outranked by the later equal-specificity '[data-medium="sheet"] .b-away' at 1283 - but the base '.b-away' at b.css:194 is ALREADY 'font-size: var(--size-body)', so line 1255 restates the inherited value below 701 and is overridden above it. It has zero effect at every width in both directions. Deleting it is lint with no pixel behind it.

The letterfit rider is the strongest part and still does not reach the bar. Four tracking tokens are declared and referenced nowhere: --track-display (-0.045em), --track-display-148, --track-title-64, --track-title-48 (the finding names three). The 148px count does render at -0.04em, the step declared for 96. But .b-num carries its tracking once at b.css:69 and the raise to 148 is a font-size-only rule, so the difference is 5.92px vs 7.40px of negative tracking on two or three tabular digits - about 4px of total width on the count, at a value that is itself a declared step, which is why audit.mjs passes it. The finding cannot say whether the answer is to wire the tokens or delete them ('or delete the three tokens'), which is the tell that no pixel is driving it. Taste-grade hygiene, correctly described, invisible at the bar.
sharpenedFix: If any of this is spent at all, spend one line: delete the four unreferenced --track-* tokens from shell.css, or wire --track-display-148 onto the 148px raise. Leave the media/container split alone - the PDF proves the artifact is invariant, and the proposed re-keying strands the measure geometry that positions the very figure it resizes.
